title: Given a `List<String>` (for example transaction reference codes), sort them by their length using `Comparator.comparingInt(String::length)`. Show ascending and how to make it descending.
shortTitle: Sort a list of strings by their length using Comparator.comparingInt(String::length)
keyPoints: comparingInt(String::length) orders strings shortest-to-longest by character count without boxing
reversed() on the comparator gives longest-first ordering
String::length is a method reference extracting the primitive int length from each string
The same derived-key technique works for any computed int property, like digit count
sorted() never mutates the source list

s1_definition.oneliner: `comparingInt(String::length)` orders strings shortest-to-longest by character count.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **`Comparator.comparingInt(String::length)`** compares by the int returned from `length()`, no boxing.
- **`reversed()`** gives longest-first ordering.
- **Tie-breaker**: `thenComparing(Comparator.naturalOrder())` sorts equal-length strings alphabetically.
- **Derived-key technique**: works for any computed int property.
- **Non-mutating**: `sorted()` produces a new stream.
s1_definition.analogy: The National Bank of India has a mix of reference codes: short legacy codes and long new UPI references. Priya wants them sorted from shortest to longest so the old short codes group together.

sections.s6_takeaway:
To sort strings by their length I use `comparingInt(String::length)`, which extracts the primitive int length with no boxing. Appending `.reversed()` gives longest-first, and `thenComparing(Comparator.naturalOrder())` makes equal-length strings alphabetical for deterministic output.

In my banking project at the National Bank of India this ordered a reconciliation report of transaction reference codes by length, letting the operations team visually separate short legacy codes from longer modern UPI and NEFT references.

The same derived-key technique generalises to any computed int property, and sorted never mutates the source list.

Remember one sentence: `comparingInt(String::length)` sorts by character count without boxing, and `.reversed()` gives longest-first.
